nodes.claim: The cascade pattern is substrate-invariant. The principle, the three paths, the dead zone — all hold when the workers are agents instead of humans.
nodes.why: The load-bearing claim of Part II. The principle from Part I survived a substrate change — sign that distributed-work-loses-context is structural, not human-specific.

nodes.claim: Three paths still hold (automate / own vertically / enable completely). Mechanics shifted: codemod-as-agent, one-operator-plus-fleet, AGENTS.md/MCP/SKILL.md as enablement primitives.
nodes.why: The action menu transfers without modification. What changed is the unit cost of each path — vertical ownership most dramatically, enablement artifact most visibly.

nodes.claim: The dead zone reproduces inside one operator. Spawn → Stall → Self-escalate → Ad-hoc merge → Cleanup campaign. Same five-step cascade, smaller scale.
nodes.why: The surprise of Part II. The org-scale cascade had multiple actors at each step — director, SVP, platform team. The single-operator version has one person occupying every role, which makes the cascade feel like personal failure rather than structural failure.

nodes.claim: Quality gates are the enablement artifact for the operator-as-reviewer. Without a trustable gate, every PR is a context-acquisition task and the operator stalls on their own work.
nodes.why: Generalizes the 'enable completely' artifact to the reviewing side of the loop. A fleet with author-side enablement (CLAUDE.md, MCP, skills) but no reviewer-side enablement (gates, coordinator, structured review) is the dead zone wearing a costume.

nodes.claim: Code production stopped being scarce; review and merge orchestration became the binding constraint. The cascade lives downstream now.
nodes.why: Names the mechanism behind D03. Throughput-shift evidence is industry-scale (Faros telemetry); the framing is Burak Dede's. The single-operator dead zone is one shape this downstream-bottleneck takes.

nodes.claim: Cloudflare's internal AI code review system: 7 specialized reviewer agents + coordinator (Opus 4.7 / GPT-5.4 judge). 131,246 runs across 48,095 MRs in 5,169 repositories, March 10 – April 9 2026.
nodes.source: Cloudflare Blog · Orchestrating AI Code Review at scale (April 2026)
nodes.why: Concrete worked example of operator-side enablement at scale. The fleet reviewing the fleet, with the human entering the loop only on judge-flagged decisions. Grounds S04.

nodes.claim: Faros AI 2026 DORA telemetry across ~22,000 developers: 98% more PRs merged with AI tools, median review time up 441% versus pre-AI baselines. Org-level DORA metrics stayed flat.
nodes.source: Faros AI · DORA Report 2025 + AI Acceleration Whiplash (2026)
nodes.why: The numbers behind D05. Throughput up at the individual level, system throughput unchanged — the binding constraint moved. Grounds D05; supports D03 indirectly.

nodes.claim: AGENTS.md (open spec, ~2026), Anthropic SKILL.md (folder + YAML frontmatter, on-demand load), Model Context Protocol (Anthropic Nov 2024, Linux Foundation Dec 2025) — three primitives for agent-readable project context.
nodes.source: agents.md / Anthropic Skills / Model Context Protocol
nodes.why: The shape of 'enable completely' for non-human readers. Three vendor-neutral or near-neutral primitives, all shipping in production by mid-2026. Grounds the enable arm of S02.

nodes.claim: Codified Context (arXiv 2602.20478): 'agents fail because they operate on inconsistent views of shared state.' Three-substrate codification — hot-memory constitution, retrieval hooks, cold-memory knowledge base — plus 19 domain-expert agents.
nodes.why: Names the same context-loss mechanism this essay names, at architecture level rather than process level. The substrate-invariance claim sits one layer up — both essays are pointing at the same loss surface.

nodes.claim: Stripe Flow→TypeScript codemod (3.7M lines in a single PR, March 6 2017; 6.5M+ lines total). Hyrum Wright's Large-Scale Changes (Software Engineering at Google, Ch 22): LSCs at Google almost always machine-generated.
nodes.source: Stripe.dev / Software Engineering at Google · Ch 22
nodes.why: Historical anchor for the automate path. The 'automate completely' arm worked pre-LLM via codemods; the LLM-era shift is in *generating* the codemod, not the path. Grounds the automate arm of S02.

eyes.what: The five-step single-operator cascade (Spawn → Stall → Self-escalate → Ad-hoc merge → Cleanup) is the author's observation. No formal study tracks the shape replicating 1:1 inside one operator.
eyes.why: Plausible from observable telemetry plus first-hand orchestration experience. External corroboration would strengthen the claim — Faros telemetry shows the symptom (review time up 441%) but not the five-step shape. Anyone surveying practitioners running fleets in 2026 would either find this shape or sharpen it.

ground_with.label: Burak Dede · The Pull Request is Dead (practitioner framing)

eyes.what: Generalizing 'enable completely' to the operator-as-reviewer is the author's extension. Cloudflare's system is one worked example; whether the framing fits other operator shapes (solo dev, two-person team, OSS maintainer) is implicit.
eyes.why: The framing reads cleanly at Cloudflare scale (130K+ MRs/month) but may compress poorly at solo-developer scale where the operator is also the consumer of the gate's output. Worth instantiating against multiple operator shapes before treating it as universal.

eyes.what: Substrate-invariance is the author's synthesis claim. Codified Context (arXiv 2602.20478) and adjacent multi-agent context-loss work name a related mechanism but do not frame the org-process cascade pattern as substrate-invariant.
eyes.why: The synthesis is novel relative to the linked prior art. If a 2025–2026 piece already names this exact framing, citing it would let Part II sit alongside that frame instead of re-naming it. Active eyes — the most likely place an external reader could already have shipped the same claim.

actions.label: Spawn the fleet
actions.body: Watch the operator's review queue saturate as N agents fan out. Demonstrates D03 and D05 — the bottleneck moves from PR creation to PR review.

actions.label: Write the gate
actions.body: Pre-merge invariants for an agent-spawned PR. Drills S04 — what the operator-side enablement artifact actually has to check.

actions.label: Audit your fleet
actions.body: For each cross-cutting task you've handed to an agent, name which of the three paths it's on. Anything you spawned without the path picked first is in the operator dead zone.

actions.label: Find the operator-side enablement gap
actions.body: Your project probably has CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md (author-side enablement). Does it have a quality gate the operator trusts (reviewer-side enablement)? If not, every agent PR is a context-acquisition task for you.

actions.label: Part I — where the cascade was first named
actions.body: How to run a cross-cutting campaign — the principle, the three paths, the cascade. Pre-LLM framing; held up under substrate change.

rubric.note: Sharper graph-discipline than Part I — every load-bearing claim cites a verifiable source, and synthesis attribution is explicit. Composite is mid not strong because the substrate-invariance claim is structural and the strongest external corroboration (Codified Context) names the mechanism without naming the framing.
rubric.soft:
Two soft spots:
1. The five-step single-operator cascade is presented as parallel structure to Part I's. Parallel framing is rhetorically clean; empirically it claims more than the citations support. Worth marking as observation rather than derivation, or surveying operators to confirm shape.
2. The 'voice survived a substrate change so the observation was structural' move is the closing claim. Strong as rhetoric; weak as proof — one substrate change is not the same as substrate-invariance. The honest read is: the principle generalizes to one new substrate; further substrates are open.
